title: operator-kms-allowlist-audit-consistency-shim
author: Priya Raman
description: Summary: Adds an operator-scoped KMS allowlist with RBAC-v2 integration and an audit consistency shim that stamps requests with a signed monotonic audit token. Motivation: customers in regulated regions require strict operator->KMS scoping and reliable audit evidence that requests were observed by the audit pipeline. This PR introduces a policy-enforced allowlist for operator service identities, ties the allowlist decision into the RBAC v2 decision flow, and attaches a lightweight audit-consistency stamp to KMS allocation requests to help downstream audit ingestion detect gaps. Changes are behind a feature flag and rolled out as a staged canary. Scope: - New RBAC hook to surface operator identity attributes into the KMS allocator. - Allowlist datastore (in-memory + persisted patch for operator-managed config) and CLI/operator-controller config. - Audit consistency shim: HMAC-signed monotonic stamp + optional proof header forwarded to audit-ingester. - Compatibility layer: non-enforced mode returns warnings and metrics; enforced mode rejects disallowed allocations. Checklist: - [x] RBAC hook added and unit tested - [x] Allowlist middleware and config docs - [x] Audit-stamp signing and verification tested in CI - [x] Canary rollout plan written and tested on staging - [x] Backwards-compatible when feature flag off Related tickets: Linear ENG-1209, ENG-1313; Support SUP-2110. Migration notes: Operators can add allowed KMS account IDs via the operator-config CRD (examples in docs/). Turning the feature flag to "enforce" will cause allocation failures for non-allowlisted operator identities; we recommend canary = 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 days while monitoring metric security.kms.allowlist.reject_rate and audit.ingest.missing_proof. Rollout: default is "warn" in 1.0.0. Monitoring & alerts: new alerts for reject_rate > 0.5% and audit-proofs-missing > 0.2% sustained for 15m. Security considerations: audit-stamp is HMAC keyed by the operator KMS signing key stored in cluster KMS; stamps are short-lived (TTL 5m) to limit replay surface. Implementation notes: RBAC v2 decision now exposes operator.zone and operator-residency-claims which the allowlist policy consults. The audit shim signs {request_id, operator_id, ts, seq} and returns X-REDWOOD-AUDIT-PROOF header; the ingest pipeline will validate HMAC and seq monotonicity per operator. Rollback: feature flag -> warn off; remove enforcement and clear reject metrics. CI/QA: end-to-end test added in perf-canary infra; manual canary run verified in us-west-2 staging.

review_comments: Carlos Mendes (2024-11-10): Please add a migration note for operator-managed clusters that use third-party KMS providers. Response: Added docs/examples and a note about provider-specific mapping in docs/security/kms-allowlist.md.

Evelyn Park (2024-11-11): Suggest verifying audit-stamp TTL is configurable; risk of high clock skew in edge regions. Response: Exposed ttlSeconds in operator_config CRD and added skew tolerance in verifier (±30s max).

Jordan Kim (2024-11-12): Tests flaky in CI for seq monotonic checks; can we add a deterministic clock in unit tests? Response: Added deterministic clock to unit tests and a flaky test marker with retry for integration tests; re-ran CI and all green.
release_notes: Add operator-scoped KMS allowlist with RBAC v2 integration and an optional audit-consistency stamp. Feature gated; default mode 'warn'. Operators must update operator_config CRD to set allowed KMS accounts for enforcement. See docs/security/kms-allowlist.md for migration and rollout guidance.
notes_for_oncall: If rollout shows reject_rate above expected, flip enforcement->warn and check operator-config for missing KMS account IDs. Audit-ingest logs will surface invalid stamps under audit.ingest.invalid_proof. Key recovery: use cluster KMS to rotate signing key and update operator-config accordingly.
canary_plan: Day 0: enable warn in staging; Day 1: canary 10% (1 cluster in prod fleet) monitor 4h; Day 2: 50% monitor 24h; Day 3: 100% enforce. Abort conditions: reject_rate > 0.5% or audit.ingest.missing_proof > 0.2% sustained 15m.
testing_notes: Unit tests for allowlist logic + stamp signer/verifier added. E2E run in perf-canary validated header flow and ingest verification. Load tests show <1ms median overhead on allocation path when stamp enabled.
